headline: Amodei denies Anthropic wants to cede control to AI
dek: According to TechCrunch and Computer Hoy, the CEO called the accusation absurd in an X post.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: The reply on X
body: Dario Amodei denied that Anthropic wants humanity to hand free will to AI (TechCrunch, Computer Hoy).
He called the suggestion absurd and said self-determination should not be sacrificed.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Where he draws the line
s3.body: For Amodei, automating tasks is not ceding control, per both outlets.

points.t: Driving, designing drugs and coding are useful automation (TechCrunch).
He admits wanting limits on AI self-improvement (Computer Hoy).
He does not expect it safe to build models unsupervised (TechCrunch).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: The post answers criticism from rival executives, including OpenAI and Meta (TechCrunch).
Amodei accused competitors of vibes-based positioning (TechCrunch).

items.t: Human control of AI is drawing attention among executives (Computer Hoy).
Anthropic leans more on AI in its own research (TechCrunch).
Altman and Wang argue for preserving human agency (TechCrunch).

caption.hook: Dario Amodei rejects the idea that Anthropic wants to cede control to AI and calls it absurd.
body: In a lengthy X post, the CEO said legitimacy and self-determination should never be sacrificed for efficiency or security, according to TechCrunch and Computer Hoy. He separates automating specific tasks from a broad surrender of human free will.

On recursive self-improvement, he acknowledged that limits may be needed. Amodei also accused rivals of using human-control language without changing their products (TechCrunch). Per Computer Hoy, the post drew close to 7 million views. The full story is at the link in bio.
caption.cta: Where should the line fall between automating tasks and keeping humans in control?
